headline: Stocks grind to a third straight gain as hike odds climb
body: The S&P 500 closed Wednesday up for a third straight session after the Federal Reserve held its policy rate steady in a split 10-2 vote, with two dissenting governors pushing for an immediate hike rather than further easing. Chair Kevin Warsh declined to pre-commit to the Fed's December meeting, and futures markets responded by pushing the implied odds of a December rate increase to roughly 85%, up from about 78% a day earlier. That is an unusual backdrop for a market still grinding toward record territory: equities climbing even as the path for rates tilts slightly more hawkish suggests investors are reading the dissent as a sign of economic resilience rather than a threat to the rally, at least for now.

Thursday's premarket tone is softer, with S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures slipping as a dense run of megacap earnings keeps the market's central tension front and center: aggressive AI capital-spending guidance versus the revenue needed to justify it. Names tied to the AI buildout are in focus as investors parse capex figures that keep climbing into the hundreds of billions, generally rewarding companies that can point to cloud or AI revenue growth and penalizing those whose spending outruns visible payoff. Retail chatter on Reddit and Stocktwits didn't surface a distinct signal beyond that same AI-spending debate already dominating headlines, so today's read leans more on price action and earnings reaction than on any fresh wave of social-media positioning.
